fatal_errors: The hypothesis omits the central intervention: atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating on SS316L followed by a 550 °C, 2 h anneal.
The proposed PWR-water and chloride tests do not reconstruct the reported 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemistry or 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot-corrosion conditions.

Neither cited study validates the claimed causal chain from heat-treatment-induced short-range ordering to surface chromium segregation, improved passive-film formation, and lower corrosion. E1 concerns N–Cr segregation at dislocations and mechanical behavior; E2 reports molten-fluoride corrosion and substantial mass loss in a different HEA.
explanation: This is a testable, broadly plausible alternative centered on chromium passivation, and its composition-matched control, surface characterization, electrochemistry, mass-loss measurements, and explicit falsification rule provide reasonable experimental discrimination. However, it is not a close reconstruction of the target. It replaces the AlCoCrFeNi APS coating and specified annealing series with an unspecified ordering treatment of generic Cr-bearing steel, uses unrelated PWR-water conditions, and misses the coating microstructure, BCC/FCC balance, grain refinement, void reduction, hardness optimum, Al-rich oxides, and molten-salt penetration mechanism. The predicted direction of reduced corrosion and the involvement of Cr-rich passive oxide overlap only at a generic level. Evidence discipline is the principal weakness: the cited findings do not support the proposed ordering-to-passivation mechanism, and heat-induced Cr segregation can also cause chromium-depleted regions or sensitization, a key competing mechanism that the design should measure directly.
